nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Why might cities prefer to use incentives instead of rules for climate action?
nodes.answer: Incentives help guide behavior without overtly controlling it, which can be beneficial when cities lack power over certain emissions sources.
nodes.subtopic: Incentives for clean energy adoption in cities

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Urban planning clean energy|Incentives for clean energy adoption in cities_qna_001
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is a significant factor that affects the effectiveness of incentive programs for high emitters in cities?
nodes.answer: High emitters must weigh whether an incentive program can adequately cover their costs to reduce emissions.
nodes.subtopic: Incentives for clean energy adoption in cities

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Urban planning clean energy|Incentives for clean energy adoption in cities_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is deemed preferable in scenarios of negative policy cost regarding rebates?
nodes.answer: A negative flat-rate charge (i.e., a lump-sum rebate) is preferable to a negative consumption surcharge in the majority of circumstances.
